findings.scenario: Observe whether WHO notices of unusual clusters, sustained human-to-human transmission, geographic spread, and health-system stress moves in the direction of concern: More sustained transmission, broader geography, greater severity, or declining response capacity
findings.observationCadence: weekly public-health scan and event-driven refresh
findings.measurableTrigger: WHO reports sustained novel transmission or a relevant preparedness gap is independently verified
findings.boundedResponse: Keep a pathogen-agnostic preparedness checklist and source-linked trigger matrix under version control
findings.rollback: Archive superseded triggers and restore the last verified checklist if evidence is retracted
findings.authorityBoundary: The automated body may monitor, model, and draft preparedness material from public sources. Medical guidance, biological experimentation, protected health data, procurement, and external coordination require separate authority and safety review; human escalation is reserved for a proven non-delegable decision.
